# Story 74 — Long conversation thread pages on the desk screen (Story: CRM-107)


---

## Review before building (GATE 2)

Checked against the code. Four things in this plan are wrong, and two of its
warnings were right where I doubted them.

**Right, and I was wrong to doubt them.** `web/src/shared/i18n/no-mirrored-styles.test.ts`
exists. `MyTicketsPage.tsx` really does carry a Previous/Next pager that
replaces its window rather than growing it — so "one page at a time" has a
precedent here, and this screen follows it rather than inventing a third
pattern. `TicketHistory` appends; both shapes are in the codebase, and a pager
is the one that answers this story's criterion.

**Wrong 1 — `page` / `pageSize` / `nextCursor`.** The API speaks `limit` and
`offset`, and answers `{ items, total, limit, offset }`. `nextCursor` is the
invention L-50 was written for; it appears here again, hedged as "or the cursor
equivalents". A hedge is not a citation. Every `page`/`pageSize` in the tasks,
the i18n block and the test plan is in a vocabulary this API does not speak.

**Wrong 2 — `?page=last`.** Offered as "preferred, if the API supports it". It
does not. There is no such shortcut and nothing in CRM-106 exposes one.

**Wrong 3 — paging past the end returns 404.** It returns `200` with an empty
page: `{"items":[],"total":0,"limit":20,"offset":999}` — checked against a
running server, not read off. So the "thread-specific 404 sentence and a
Go to newest action" is a screen built for an answer the API never gives.

**Wrong 4 — `ticketThread.pager.empty`.** `ticketThread.emptyTitle` and
`emptyBody` already exist and are already rendered by `EmptyState`. A third
string for the same case is the drift BR-6 exists to stop.

**One thing the plan did not know, because it is a defect in code shipped an
hour before it was generated.** `CONVERSATION-2-WEB (CRM-103)` left
`useTicketThread` appending at `offset = messages.length` behind a button
reading **"Show older messages"**. The thread is oldest first, so that offset
fetches the NEWER page: the button did the opposite of what it said. Nothing
caught it — the test asserted the older page arrived, not that it was older.
That is this story's real work, alongside the landing page.

**What is built instead.** One page at a time, Previous/Next, landing on the
last page. The step comes from the answer's own `limit` rather than a
`PAGE_SIZE` the screen picks: `MyTicketsPage` sends `?limit=${PAGE_SIZE}`, and
this hook deliberately does not — the window is the API's, and paging by the
number it just reported keeps it that way. Landing on the newest costs a second
request on a long thread, because `total` is not knowable before the first
answer and no shortcut exists; on a thread that fits one page it costs nothing.

## Prerequisites

- `CONVERSATION-1-API` shipped — the desk thread endpoint returns a paged window (page/pageSize/total or nextCursor). Coordinate with `CONVERSATION-4-API (CRM-106)` for the exact wire shape; do not add filtering the API does not expose.
- Sibling frontend paging precedents already merged: `web/src/pages/portal/MyTicketsPage.tsx` (+ `useMyTickets.ts`) and `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketHistory.tsx` (+ `useTicketHistory.ts`). This story follows the **API's window, not the screen's** convention those files established.

## Story Goal

A long ticket conversation thread in the desk (agent-facing `TicketThread`) is paged on screen using the API's window — the screen never asks for more than one page at a time, never concatenates all pages into an unbounded list, and never re-implements ordering, filtering, or sizing the API already owns (BR-4).

Because the thread is ordered **oldest-first**, the reader who opens a long thread almost always wants the **newest** message. The screen therefore lands on the **last page** by default, with a visible reason (e.g. a "newest first" affordance / paging control that shows which page you are on and lets you page back through history). Every visible string comes from `en.ts` and `ar.ts` (BR-6).

Explicitly out of scope: any change under `api/` — those belong to `CONVERSATION-4-API (CRM-106)`.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current:** `TicketThread` renders whatever the thread endpoint returned in one pass. On a long thread this either blows past the API window silently or presents the oldest messages first with no way to reach the newest.
- **New (BR-4):** the screen displays exactly one API page at a time; page size and ordering are the API's; the screen adds no client-side sort or filter. A pager surfaces `Page X of Y` and previous/next controls. The initial landing page is the **last** page (newest messages), and the UI names why ("Showing newest — page X of Y", both languages).
- **New (BR-6):** no literal user-visible strings in JSX; every label, aria-label, and separator text lives in `en.ts`/`ar.ts` under a new nested group (e.g. `ticketThread.pager`).

## Frontend Tasks

### 1 — Extend `useTicketThread` to consume the API's window

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/useTicketThread.ts`

- Accept a `page` argument (1-indexed) and optionally `pageSize` **only if** the endpoint accepts them; otherwise pass through whatever cursor field the API layer defined in `CONVERSATION-4-API (CRM-106)`. Use the exact query-parameter names the API contract publishes — grep `useMyTickets.ts` / `useTicketHistory.ts` for the naming convention already in use before adding new ones.
- Keep the `useRequest` four-state contract. The success payload the hook exposes must include:
  - `messages` — the page's items in the order the API returned them (do not re-sort on the client).
  - `page`, `pageSize`, `total` (or the cursor equivalents the API uses).
  - `totalPages` — derive from `total` / `pageSize` **only** when `total` is present; otherwise expose the cursor fields verbatim.
- Do **not** merge pages into a growing array. Each page load replaces the previous window (the API's window, not the screen's).
- Do **not** call `request()` with a hard-coded `/api/v1` prefix (`shared/api/base-url.ts` already prefixes it).

### 2 — Render one page with a pager in `TicketThread`

**File:** `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketThread.tsx`

- On first mount for a given ticket, request the **last** page: fetch page 1 first only to learn `total`/`totalPages`, then request `totalPages` — **or**, preferred, add a `?page=last` shortcut in the hook that resolves to the last page in a single request if the API supports it. Choose whichever the API contract from CRM-106 exposes; do not invent one.
- Render exactly the messages in `messages` for the current page. Do not append; do not sort; do not filter.
- Add a pager control below (or above, matching the RTL/LTR conventions already used in `MyTicketsPage.tsx`) with:
  - "Previous" button — disabled when `page === 1`.
  - "Next" button — disabled when `page === totalPages`.
  - A status line: `"Showing newest — page {page} of {totalPages}"` when landed on the last page; `"Page {page} of {totalPages}"` on any other page.
- All numeric values interpolated into a translated sentence must be wrapped with the bidi isolate helper used by `pages/tickets/history-sentence.ts` (U+2068 … U+2069, L-51).
- Preserve existing loading and error states via `useRequest`'s `idle | loading | success | error` machine. Reuse `t.errors[code]` **only** after reading the shared sentence; if the shared one misreads the situation (e.g. a 404 on a paged-past-the-end request), add a thread-specific sentence in `en.ts`/`ar.ts` rather than reusing a wrong default.

### 3 — Wire the way in

- If any test or route currently loads `TicketThread` at page 0 or with all messages, update it to match the new default (last-page landing) so the desk agent's normal navigation reaches the newest message in one click — a route only its author can navigate to is a route that does not exist.
- Grep for `useTicketThread` callers; update each to pass the new `page` argument (or the "last page" sentinel), and ensure the paging control is visible on the parent screen — not hidden behind a scroll or a modal footer.

### 4 — i18n keys (BR-6)

**Files:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`

Add, in the **same commit**, a nested group under `ticketThread` (or extend the existing group if one exists — grep before adding):

```ts
ticketThread: {
  pager: {
    previous: 'Previous',        // ar: 'السابق'
    next: 'Next',                // ar: 'التالي'
    pageOfTotal: 'Page {page} of {total}',
    showingNewest: 'Showing newest — page {page} of {total}',
    empty: 'No messages in this thread yet.',
  },
},
```

- Keep leaves camelCase, one level deep, matching `en.ts` conventions.
- Do **not** use a template function; interpolation is done at the call site by splicing the value with a bidi isolate wrapper, as `history-sentence.ts` does.
- The separator "—" between the two clauses of `showingNewest` must live inside the resource string, **not** typed between JSX tags (or `pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` will fail).

### 5 — No native validators / no browser-owned rules

- The pager uses buttons, not `<input type="number" min max>`. Do not let the browser own the "which page is valid" rule.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Single-page thread (`totalPages === 1`).** Render the messages; hide (or disable and label) both pager buttons; status line reads `Page 1 of 1`. Enforced in `TicketThread.tsx` pager render branch.
- **Empty thread (`total === 0`).** Render the `ticketThread.pager.empty` string; do not render the pager. Enforced in `TicketThread.tsx`.
- **Reader pages past the end** (e.g. race with a message being deleted server-side). The API returns 404 or an empty page — show a thread-specific sentence and a "Go to newest" action that jumps back to `totalPages`. Do not reuse a generic `t.errors[404]` that reads as "not found" for the whole ticket.
- **Ticket has grown while the reader was on an old page.** `totalPages` has moved. When Next is clicked, re-request; if the returned `page` no longer matches what was asked for, trust the API's `page` field and update the pager, not the local intent.
- **RTL (Arabic).** Previous/Next visual order follows the document direction that `shared/i18n/index.tsx` already sets. Do not mirror with CSS transforms (`no-mirrored-styles.test.ts` will catch it).
- **Interpolated page numbers in Arabic sentence.** Wrap the numeric value in U+2068 … U+2069 (L-51) so the digits do not scramble the surrounding text.
- **Fetch stub in tests.** Every stubbed request must build a **fresh** `Response` per call (L-30) — a shared `Response` cannot be read twice, and paging tests read it many times.
- **Desk-shell dependency.** `TicketThread` mounts inside the desk shell, which asks `/me`; every test must stub `/me` via `src/testing/stub-me.ts` or the shell fails to render.
- **API contract drift.** If CRM-106 exposes cursors instead of `page`/`total`, the pager's status sentence changes ("Newer messages ›" / "‹ Older messages") — resolve by reading the CRM-106 plan and matching its field names. Do not hard-code assumptions.

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema change; feature is purely UI + hook. Rollback = revert the `TicketThread.tsx`, `useTicketThread.ts`, `TicketThread.css`, `en.ts`, `ar.ts`, and test edits in one commit. No data on disk changes.
- Half-applied risk: shipping the hook change without the pager UI would silently drop older messages. Ship the two together; guard with the new test in item 1.

4. **Backend regression:** `cd api && npm test` — must remain green; this story does not touch `api/` and any change there indicates an accidental edit.
5. **Regression — no AI attribution anywhere:** `git grep -nE -i "(claude|copilot|chatgpt|openai|anthropic|ai[- ]assist)" -- . ':!*.lock'` returns no matches in modified files.
6. **Manual smoke:** run `cd api && npm start` in one shell and `cd web && npm run dev` in another; open a ticket with > 1 page of messages as an agent; confirm the screen lands on the last page, the status line names it, Prev/Next work, and Arabic reads correctly (digits stay attached to the correct clause).

**Not built, and why.** Four items in the tasks above describe an API that does
not exist and were not built: `page`/`pageSize`/`nextCursor` (the API speaks
`limit` and `offset`), the `?page=last` shortcut, the 404-past-the-end sentence
and its "Go to newest" action (past the end is `200` with an empty page), and
`ticketThread.pager.empty` (`emptyTitle`/`emptyBody` already exist and already
render). Each is argued in **Review before building** above.

Two things were built that the plan did not ask for, because the code it was
planned against was an hour old and wrong:

- The **"Show older messages" button fetched newer messages.** It appended at
  `offset = messages.length` in an oldest-first thread. Its test asserted a page
  arrived, not that the page was older.
- The pager reads **messages, not pages** — "the newest messages: 21 to 40 of
  40". A page number is a number the screen would have invented; the window is
  what the API actually answered with, and it survives a page size the server
  changes.

Six mutations were run against the new tests. Landing on the oldest page fails
6, reversing `older` fails 4, sending a limit of the screen's own fails 1,
showing a new message on every page fails 1, dropping the isolate fails 1, and
showing the pager on a single-page thread fails 1.

**STOP HERE. Report to the user and wait for confirmation before proceeding to the next story.**
